title: Purser common definitions
description: Shared definitions referenced by every other contract: money, exact decimals, identifiers, timestamps, evidence tiers (architecture 6.5), and evidenced values. String formats listed under $defs are the only patterned strings the no-free-text lint accepts in event schemas (C2, C4); each is bounded and admits no whitespace. This document validates nothing on its own.

schema_version.description: Version of the contract an instance conforms to. Any 0.1.x instance is valid under the 0.1.0 schemas.

uuid.description: Lowercase RFC 9562 UUID text form. Used for attempt, decision, and event IDs.

id.description: Opaque identifier (org, workspace, team, user, device, virtual key, route, window, session, prompt, provider request, price-book version, key, fee). Letters, digits, and . _ : - only: no whitespace, so it cannot hold prose.

model_id.description: Provider model identifier, such as claude-opus-5-5 or anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (OpenRouter). Adds / @ + to the id alphabet.

semver.description: Dotted numeric version with an optional pre-release suffix, such as 2.1.285 or 0.48.0-beta.1.

rfc3339_utc.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with a Z suffix and up to nanosecond precision. The pattern enforces it; format is an annotation only.

decimal.description: Exact non-negative decimal as a string (architecture 6.4): rates in USD per million tokens, multipliers, fees, and USD amounts. No sign, exponent, or leading zeros. Never a JSON number.

probability.description: Exact decimal probability in [0, 1] as a string.

delta_seconds.description: Non-negative integer seconds as an HTTP header value (retry-after, RFC 9110 delay-seconds).

https_url.description: Absolute https URL, used only for dated price sources. Not allowed in event schemas.

nanodollars.description: Money in integer nano-dollars (1 nd = $0.000000001), non-negative, signed 64-bit range (architecture 6.4). JSON Schema's integer type also matches 209000000.0, so producers must write integers and consumers must parse with a reader that rejects floats (as contracts/tools/check_contracts.py does) and keeps 64-bit integers exact: above 2^53 an IEEE double loses precision.

signed_nanodollars.description: Money in integer nano-dollars that can be negative, such as remaining budget after an overrun (architecture 7.6).

provider.description: Upstream provider. local is a model reached directly by the sidecar (metered, never billed).

harness.description: Agent harness (architecture 1 G1, 5, 6.6). kiro and pi have trace readers only.

evidence_tier.description: Evidence tier for a value (architecture 6.5). unavailable means the source cannot provide the value; it is never the same as a measured zero.

unavailable_reason.description: Why a value is unavailable. not_reported: the source does not provide it. not_applicable: the dimension does not exist for this provider or path. stream_interrupted: lost when the stream was cut. usage_unavailable: no usage was obtained, so cost cannot be computed. pending_reconciliation: waiting for provider billing data. unpriced: the price book does not cover the attempt (6.3). not_billed: a local model, metered but never billed. unrecognized_format: a trace format the reader does not recognize (6.6). unrecognized_value: a request or response value outside the enumerated set; the raw value is not stored (C2). no_response: the attempt produced no response.

evidence_rules.$comment: Applied with allOf to every evidenced value: unavailable evidence holds exactly when value is null, and unavailable_reason is present exactly then.

evidenced_count.description: A token or use count with its evidence tier.

evidenced_duration_ms.description: A duration with its evidence tier.

evidenced_id.description: An identifier with its evidence tier.

evidenced_model_id.description: A model identifier with its evidence tier.

evidenced_semver.description: A version with its evidence tier.

evidenced_timestamp.description: A timestamp with its evidence tier.

hmac.description: Keyed hash of a provider message or response ID (architecture 6.6, improvement 2): HMAC-SHA256 under a per-org key, so the relay and trace readers compute the same value and the raw ID is never stored.

evidenced_hmac.description: A keyed hash with its evidence tier; unavailable when the source carries no provider ID.
